newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: American Airlines interested in Argentine carriers.
newsitem.headline: American Airlines interested in Argentine carriers.

text.p: AMR Corp's American Airlines is interested in buying Argentine carriers Aerolineas Argentinas and Austral, state-owned news agency Telam quoted former U.S. ambassador to Argentina James Cheek as saying on Wednesday.

Cheek, an adviser to the U.S. airline, made the statements after a meeting with Argentine President Carlos Menem, Telam said. Also present at the meeting were American's international planning manager, David Cush, and the regional manager, Diego Cousino.

It will not be long before Merrill Lynch "has the initial offer - it is no easy thing to buy an airline, it is a big task for American, there are many people working on this, including myself," Telam quoted Cheek as saying.
Menem considered American a good partner for Aerolineas, he added.

The largest shareholder in Aerolineas, with a 63 percent stake, is Andes Holding, which is in turn owned by Merrill Lynch, Bankers Trust and the Spanish government's holding company, Teneo. The Spanish government's stake amounts to around 45 percent.
Speculation around potential buyers of Aerolineas has hotted up in recent months. Aerolineas has said it was in talks with American and other U.S. airlines on a possible code-sharing deal.
Continental Airlines Inc has also stated it is interested in a stake in Aerolineas.
Cheek acknowledged there were other interested buyers but said he was sure "nobody will make a better offer than American."
